newsitem.title: USA: Revlon holding company weighs debt options.
newsitem.headline: Revlon holding company weighs debt options.

text.p: Revlon Worldwide Corp said it would consider selling additional Revlon Inc shares or refinancing its debt to pay off its $1.1 billion worth of zero-coupon bonds due March 1998.
William Fox, Revlon Inc chief financial officer and executive vice president, told Reuters all options are under consideration but the company has not yet made a decision.
"We've always had these choices," he said. "The value and the alternatives are there."
He also said holders of Revlon Inc shares should not be nervous about the debt of its holding company, Revlon Worldwide.
"We hear virtually nothing about nervous...the Revlon Inc bonds couldn't go any higher," he said.

The company declined comment on rumors among junk bond traders that the holding company would do an early refinancing of the debt, timed to take advantage of Revlon Inc's year-end earnings, which are expected to be strong.
Revlon shares were up 1/2 to 32-5/8. In November the stock was at its year high of 36-1/2.

Investors have kept an eye on the stock after Ron Perelman, who owns 83 percent of Revlon's shares, helped send Marvel Entertainment Group Inc into bankruptcy in the midst of a battle with Marvel's bondholders.
Perelman owns his stake in Revlon through Revlon Worldwide Corp, which is part of holding company MacAndrews & Forbes.

Revlon Inc Chairman and Chief Executive Jerry Levin said the cosmetics company was legally protected from Revlon Worldwide's zero-note debt and had its own $1.5 billion in long-term debt under control.
"Revlon Inc, we don't have any debt due for a long time. Our cash flow is strong. There is literally no concern," Levin said. "There really is no issue. There is no connection."

In its most recent 10-Q filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission, Revlon Worldwide said it expects to adopt one or more of the following alternatives for its zero notes: refinancing, seeking capital contributions or loans from affiliates, or selling additional shares of capital stock of Revlon Inc.
An offering of Revlon Inc shares could dilute the share value, but Fox said the company's year-end results would make the additional shares manageable.

Revlon, which is expected to report fourth-quarter earnings around the end of the month, has said it expects to meet its quarterly estimate of $0.55 per share based on strong sales from its ColorStay and Almay product lines.
